narrative.overview:
Sky looks like a crew instrument that is watching, not like a dashboard wearing a space theme. The field is a deep navy that grades from a lit halo at the top of the viewport down to near-black; information sits on glass panels that float just above it; one sea-glass teal marks the thing that is currently actionable. Nothing else competes. Presence is carried by a single luminous object — the orb — and by the quality of attention in the copy, never by decoration.

The system is dark-only and it is a reading surface more than a browsing one: an astronaut glances, understands what changed, and answers once. That is why types are light-weight, why measurements are tabular, why labels are small letter-spaced caps, and why the accent is rationed. Depth comes from tonal gradients and 1px translucent cyan borders, not from drop shadows.

Two registers share one identity. The stage register is the HUD, the cinematic routes and the two data faces: radial backdrop, glass cards, glow accents. The instrument register is where an operator completes a task (admin, the crew picker, the watch face): flat fills, solid slate borders, real shadows, 14px type. Both use the same palette and the same sea-glass accent.
keyCharacteristics: Deep navy radial stage (#010812 → #091c32 → #0c3159), never pure black except on the watch face.
One primary accent — sea-glass teal (#5eead4) — plus an instrument cyan and a violet that appears only inside gradients and rims.
Glass panels: 18px radius, 1px rgba(122,222,255,.15) border, gradient fill, 8px backdrop blur, 1px inset top highlight.
Light-weight type (300) at every size; uppercase micro-labels at 9–11px with .14–.2em tracking; tabular numerals for every measurement.
Pills for all chrome (chips, tabs, tags, voice controls); asymmetric organic radii only for glass cutouts.
Depth by glow and tonal layering, not by shadow.
SIMULATED is always visible on fixture data; every threshold and score carries its source.

rules.name: The One Bright Object Rule
rules.body: Exactly one luminous focal object per screen: the orb, or the body hologram, or an open decision — never two. When the decision is active, the orb dims; when the body is active, the orb steps back.

rules.name: The Rare Teal Rule
rules.body: Sea-glass teal appears on ≤10% of any screen. Its rarity is what makes it read as "this is the thing to act on". Painting every number teal destroys the only hierarchy signal the system has.

rules.name: The Gradient-Rim Rule
rules.body: Multi-hue gradients (teal → blue → violet, or teal → violet) live only in a 1px rim, an arc, a progress fill, or the around-a-pill border technique — never as the fill of a surface, never on text.

rules.name: The Light-Weight Rule
rules.body: Interface text is font-weight 300; 400 is for micro-labels, 500 for uppercase labels, 600 only for the two button roles and crew names. A 700-weight headline is a different product.

rules.name: The Micro-Label Rule
rules.body: Uppercase with .14–.2em tracking is allowed only at ≤11px and only for labels, chips, and stamps. Setting a sentence in tracked caps is the anti-pattern the whole system was built to avoid.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every measurement, delta, countdown and score is tabular-nums; every unit is a separate small span in text-muted. Numbers never animate between values.

rules.name: The Glow-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: On the stage, an element is raised by a tonal gradient and a glow — never by a grey drop shadow. A grey shadow on the navy field reads as dirt.

rules.name: The One Halo Rule
rules.body: At most one element per screen carries a coloured outer bloom. Two competing halos is the visual signature of a HUD mock, not of an instrument.

rules.name: The Pill-For-Chrome Rule
rules.body: If it is chrome, it is a pill; if it holds content, it is a rounded rectangle. A square button in the HUD, or a pill around a card, is a register error.

rules.name: The One Aperture Rule
rules.body: One organic cutout per screen, and only around a subject that carries data. A second organic shape turns an instrument into a poster.

dos: Do keep one bright object per screen; dim the orb when the readiness panel or a decision is the focus.
Do spend sea-glass teal on the actionable element only, and keep it under ~10% of the surface.
Do build panels from gradient fill + 1px alpha-cyan border + inset top highlight; add backdrop blur only where the stage shows through.
Do keep every measurement tabular, with its unit separate and muted, and every score labelled with its source or SIMULATED.
Do show the SIMULATED chip on any fixture value, on the card itself, at ≥8.5px — never only in a footer.
Do keep the focus ring at 2px #f5fcff, offset 3–5px, on every interactive element including canvases and the picker.
Do ship both languages through shared/i18n and let the widest string drive the layout.
Do give every state a word, not only a colour: unknown, stale, queued, acknowledged, needs review.
Do treat reduced motion as a first-class state: no animation and instant state changes when it is requested.
donts: Do not add a webfont, CDN stylesheet, or remote image for the app's own chrome — the type stack resolving to the platform face is the system. The vendored React Bits VariableProximity label (Roboto Flex via Google Fonts) is the one exception, on the declarative HUD — not a precedent.
Do not use red or amber to dramatise AI text, a delta, or a trend; coral is for reviewed critical states only, and a 30-day delta is neutral teal.
Do not paint a card with a violet or purple gradient; violet lives in rims, arcs and the thinking halo.
Do not use a purple–cyan gradient as a surface fill, a glowing rectangle around every card, a left sidebar, or a 4–8 equal-KPI grid — those are the anti-references this system exists to refuse.
Do not set body text in tracked uppercase, use 700 weights, or drop any readable text below 8.5px.
Do not animate numbers between values, simulate a waveform from nothing, or leave an infinite idle animation beyond the slow orb drift and the chest glow.
Do not add a third backdrop to the console, another device view behind a query param, or a second organic aperture to one screen.
Do not let a generated label or an LLM author a threshold, a severity, or a stable/safe verdict; absence renders as unknown, never as green.
Do not treat acknowledgement as resolution, confirmation as performance, or queued as transmitted.
